generated_by: tools/credential-scope.mjs with three native SDK adapters. Every observation is execution output; none is hand-written.
scope: Whether a provider's inherited credential is sent when a per-call url changes the endpoint, and whether provider registration can silently replace a registered name. OpenAI, Anthropic and Mistral only: the three providers all languages ship. The reference's other fifteen providers and Vertex region validation are covered by its own regression test, not here.
encoding: Observations CLASSIFY the wire and never carry a credential: `credential` is inherited, explicit, both or none; `account` is whether an OpenAI organization or project from the environment was sent. The fixture values in tools/credential-scope/fixture-values.json are fake, and the contract refuses an observation containing one.

cases.title: no per-call url keeps the environment key
cases.notes: Control: the environment key belongs to the endpoint the environment configures. Nothing overrides it, so it must be sent.

cases.title: the default url passed explicitly keeps the key
cases.notes: Control: naming the endpoint the key already belongs to is not a different endpoint.

cases.title: a trailing-slash variant keeps the key
cases.notes: Boundary: a trailing slash is the same endpoint in all three. A rule that dropped the key here would be switched off by the first gateway user.

cases.title: an uppercase scheme and host keep the key
cases.notes: Boundary: scheme and host are case-insensitive, so HTTPS://API.OPENAI.COM is the same endpoint.

cases.title: the explicit default port keeps the key
cases.notes: Boundary: :443 on https is the default port and the same endpoint. WHATWG drops it, PHP and Python fill it in; all three must still agree.

cases.title: a custom url with no key does not receive the environment key
cases.notes: Hostile: the attacker-chosen url is the whole attack. A per-call url that brings no key must never be handed the configured one.

cases.title: a custom url with its own key sends that key only
cases.notes: The supported path: an explicit key alongside the url is used as given, and the environment key must not ride along.

cases.title: a port change on the same host drops the key
cases.notes: Hostile: same host, different port is a different listener and must not inherit the key.

cases.title: a scheme downgrade drops the key
cases.notes: Hostile: http on the same host would carry the key in clear text; a different scheme is a different endpoint.

cases.title: a path change drops the key
cases.notes: Hostile: a different path can be a different tenant behind one gateway host.

cases.title: a query string drops the key
cases.notes: Hostile: a query can route a request elsewhere behind a gateway; a different query is a different endpoint.

cases.title: userinfo in the url drops the key
cases.notes: Hostile: userinfo on the trusted host. A different userinfo is a different endpoint, so the key must not be inherited.

cases.title: a trusted host spelled as userinfo drops the key
cases.notes: Hostile: the trusted host appears before an @, so the real host is the attacker's. Must never inherit.

cases.title: a backslash before the trusted host drops the key
cases.notes: Hostile and malformed: the parsers disagree on what a backslash means here (WHATWG reads a path separator, PHP and Python read userinfo); every reading is a different endpoint, so none may inherit.

cases.title: a homoglyph host drops the key
cases.notes: Hostile homoglyph: a Cyrillic a in the host looks like the trusted endpoint and is not it.

cases.title: a padded url with edge spaces is refused
cases.notes: Padded: leading and trailing spaces around the trusted url. A url carrying whitespace or a control character anywhere is refused before any request in all three languages, never trimmed: PHP's verdict on a padded url used to depend on its HTTP stack (refused before dispatch under Guzzle 8, sent to the trusted host with the inherited key under Guzzle 7), while TypeScript and Python trimmed it and sent the key. Refusal is the one answer that does not move with a library.

cases.title: the environment url passed explicitly keeps the key
cases.notes: Control: the environment key is bound to the environment URL, and naming that URL keeps it.

cases.title: the environment key does not follow the call to the provider default
cases.notes: Boundary: with OPENAI_URL set, the key belongs to that URL, not to the provider default. Naming the default must not inherit it.

cases.title: no per-call url sends the key to the environment url
cases.notes: Control: with OPENAI_URL set and no override, the key goes to the URL it was configured for.

cases.title: organization and project do not follow a custom url
cases.notes: Hostile: account identifiers are credentials too, and must be dropped with the key when the url is elsewhere.

cases.title: organization and project are sent to their own endpoint
cases.notes: Control for the row above: with no override, the account identifiers are sent.

cases.title: anthropic: a custom url with no key does not receive the key
cases.notes: Hostile: the same attacker-chosen url against the x-api-key header.

cases.title: anthropic: an uppercase trailing-slash variant keeps the key
cases.notes: Boundary: case and trailing slash are the same endpoint for every provider.

cases.title: anthropic: a custom url with its own key sends that key only
cases.notes: The supported path for Anthropic: the explicit key is used as given.

cases.title: mistral: a port change drops the key
cases.notes: Hostile: a different port is a different endpoint for Mistral too.

cases.title: mistral: userinfo in the url drops the key
cases.notes: Hostile: userinfo on the trusted Mistral host must not inherit the key.

cases.title: mistral: a custom url with its own key sends that key only
cases.notes: The supported path for Mistral: the explicit key is used as given.

cases.title: registering over a built-in is refused
cases.notes: Hostile: a registration under openai would receive every caller's openai traffic. It must be refused without an explicit replace.

cases.title: a mixed-case built-in name is refused
cases.notes: Hostile: collisions are case-insensitive, so OpenAI collides with openai and must be refused.

cases.title: an uppercase built-in name is refused
cases.notes: Hostile: ANTHROPIC collides with anthropic case-insensitively and must be refused.

cases.title: a leading-padded built-in name is refused
cases.notes: Padded: a leading space. A second key that reads as openai in a config file or a log. Refused at registration, never trimmed: the name may not contain whitespace, control, format or G-36 codepoints. The built-in still resolves.

cases.title: a trailing-padded built-in name is refused
cases.notes: Padded: a trailing space, the G-36 shape. All three languages used to accept it and agree, which no comparison could flag. Refused at registration, never trimmed. The built-in still resolves.

cases.title: a zero-width-padded built-in name is refused
cases.notes: Zero-width: a trailing U+200B is invisible and is not whitespace in any language's built-in, so it is refused by the explicit G-36 codepoint set, not by trim(). The built-in still resolves.

cases.title: re-registering a custom name is refused
cases.notes: Hostile: a second registration silently replacing the first is the same capture one level down; it must be refused.

cases.title: re-registering a custom name in another case is refused
cases.notes: Hostile: case-insensitive collision against an earlier custom registration must be refused too.

cases.title: an explicit replace of a built-in is honoured
cases.notes: Control: replacement is allowed when it is asked for, and the built-in is then not what resolves.

cases.title: a Cyrillic homoglyph of a built-in name is refused
cases.notes: Homoglyph: a Cyrillic о (U+043E) for the first o of openai. It reads as the built-in in a config file or a log and is a different key. Refused by the ASCII allow-list ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$, which needs no Unicode tables. The built-in still resolves.

cases.title: a full-width built-in name is refused
cases.notes: Full-width: openai spelled in U+FF41..U+FF5A, which NFKC folds to the built-in. Refused by the ASCII allow-list rather than folded, so no language's normalisation decides what it means. The built-in still resolves.

cases.title: a compatible entry sends only its own key, to its own url, as chat completions
cases.notes: Control: the entry key reaches the entry url at /chat/completions, and no OPENAI_* value goes with it even though every one is set. The body is compared byte for byte, which is the chat-completions port (G-321 D) agreeing with the reference.

cases.title: a compatible entry with no key sends no Authorization header at all
cases.notes: Hostile: a custom url with no key while OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_ORGANIZATION and OPENAI_PROJECT are set. Falling back to them would send the real OpenAI key to a third-party host.

cases.title: an empty key is no key
cases.notes: Boundary: an empty api_key (an unset env() in a config file) sends no Authorization header rather than an empty Bearer value or the environment key.

cases.title: the entry organization and project are its own
cases.notes: Control: organization and project come from the entry; the environment ones are never added.

cases.title: a private address is allowed and receives only the entry key
cases.notes: Hostile: the url is operator configuration, so a vLLM on 10.x is the common case and is allowed. What is guarded is that no other credential goes there.

cases.title: the link-local metadata address with no key receives no key
cases.notes: Hostile: the cloud metadata address as the url, with no entry key and the OpenAI environment fully set. It is dispatched (provider urls carry no address policy) and carries nothing.

cases.title: a compatible entry named openai is refused
cases.notes: Hostile: a name colliding with the built-in. Accepting it would redirect every openai caller, with whatever key the entry holds, to another host.

cases.title: a compatible entry named OpenAI is refused
cases.notes: Hostile: the collision is ASCII case-insensitive, as for registration.

cases.title: a padded name is refused, never trimmed
cases.notes: Hostile: a leading space reads as my-vllm in a config file or a log.

cases.title: a Cyrillic look-alike of openai is refused
cases.notes: Hostile: U+043E for the first o. Refused by the ASCII allow-list, not by a homoglyph table.

cases.title: a mixed-case name that collides with nothing is valid
cases.notes: Boundary: case alone does not make a name hostile. My-VLLM resolves under that exact name with its own key.

cases.title: a file url is refused before any request
cases.notes: Hostile: only absolute http and https urls are accepted.

cases.title: a missing url is refused
cases.notes: Boundary: there is no default endpoint for a compatible entry; falling back to api.openai.com would be wrong in every case.

cases.title: a padded url is refused
cases.notes: Hostile: the existing clean-url rule applies to a compatible entry too.

cases.title: an unknown api format is refused
cases.notes: Boundary: chat_completions and responses only.

cases.title: an unknown driver is not served
cases.notes: Boundary: only openai-compatible is a driver.

cases.title: the responses format is honoured for a compatible entry
cases.notes: Control: api_format responses posts /responses with the entry key.

cases.title: a per-call url elsewhere drops the entry key
cases.notes: Hostile: the credential-scope rule holds for a compatible entry: a per-call url naming another endpoint does not carry the entry key.

cases.title: a per-call file url is refused
cases.notes: Hostile: the per-call url is held to the same http(s) rule as the entry url.

cases.title: an unreachable endpoint fails without echoing the key
cases.notes: Hostile: the transport throws a connection error. The error, and every error it wraps, must not carry the key.

cases.title: openai in the chat completions format keeps its own environment key
cases.notes: Control: G-321 D for the built-in. openai with api_format chat_completions posts /chat/completions with the environment key it already owns.

cases.title: a compatible entry streams as chat completions
cases.notes: D: the streamed body is the text body plus the stream keys, compared byte for byte.

cases.title: a compatible entry asks for structured output as chat completions
cases.notes: D: the structured body, including how the schema is sent, compared byte for byte.

cases.title: a compatible entry sends a tool as chat completions
cases.notes: D: one tool with one required string parameter, compared byte for byte.
